author: IGN
description:
We’re over halfway through 2026 already, which means it’s time to check in on all of Sony’s PlayStation Studios to see what they’re making and what PS5 games are coming in 2026 and beyond. While the PS5 has received many great third-party releases so far this year, such as Resident Evil Requiem, 007 First Light, and Crimson Desert, only one first-party game has made its way into our hands: Housemarque’s latest shooter, Saros. It’s hard to ignore the biggest PlayStation news of the year so far, though: the decision to end the production of discs from January 2028, which leaves a big question mark over whether we’ll ever get physical editions of some of the games we’re about to talk about here.

So, which PlayStation studios have games launching soon, or at the very least have secrets up their sleeves? Well, that’s exactly what we’re going to take a look at here. What are the developers behind PlayStation’s highly respected library up to now? And how long will it be before we get to bot
title: The State of Every PlayStation Studio - Summer 2026

author: IGN
description: "Sometimes Spider-Man has to do the hard thing, even if it breaks Peter Parker's heart." After the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home, the world has forgotten Peter Parker, and he's spent years trying to keep it that way. But Spider-Man: Brand New Day follows Peter as he starts to reach back out to his old friends in the face of a new enemy. IGN's Tom Jorgensen spoke with producers Kevin Feige and Amy Pascal, director Destin Daniel Cretton, and actors Tom Holland, Jon Bernthal, and Jacob Batalon about how Peter is fighting through loneliness, and how Brand New Day could serve as a "beacon of hope" to those dealing with it themselves.
title: Is Spider-Man: Brand New Day About The Male Loneliness Epidemic?

author: IGN
description:
Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game reviewed by Mitchell Saltzman on PC, also coming to PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 1 & 2

The potential of Avatar Legends is immense. This is a gorgeous 2D fighting game that excels as both a throwback to the bygone era of sprite-based fighters and a faithful adaptation of the beloved cartoons it’s based on. It’s got some of the most satisfying movement of any 2D fighter I’ve played, combos routes that are challenging but immensely rewarding to learn, a 12 character roster that feels way bigger than it actually is thanks to the clever support system, and flexible combat that allows for a ton of creative expression. The lackluster story mode, complete absence of some basic options like difficulty settings for the CPU, and lack of a guided tutorial to teach you how to actually play certainly make Avatar Legends hard to recommend to casual Avatar fans, but for fighting game fans looking for something with “the sauce,” Avatar Legends
title: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game Review

author: IGN
description:
If you’ve built a Pal Labor Research Lab and suddenly find yourself in desperate need of Mysterious Mushrooms, don’t panic! Finding this rare fungi can be confusing after dozens of hours of playing, but we have everything you need to know about what these mushy bits are and where you can get your hands on them.

Mysterious Mushrooms are a material and currency used almost exclusively in the Pal Labor Research Lab perk trees to gain passive benefits and unlock inaccessible schematics. To farm Mysterious Mushrooms in large quantities, you will need to travel to the Sakurajima island in the far northwest of the map. In the southeast part of this Japan-themed region, you can harvest massive mushrooms with an ax to get the resource. Be careful, as the journey is filled with high-level enemies and deadly Pals, so bring a flying Pal to help you navigate the danger and harvest your Mysterious Mushrooms safely.

#ign #gaming #palworld
title: Where to Farm Mysterious Mushrooms in Palworld 1.0

author: IGN
description:
Take a look at gameplay from Langrisser: Sea of Sword in this latest trailer for the next fantasy tactical RPG in the Langrisser series. Learn about the character and see tactical gameplay from Langrisser: Sea of Sword in this new trailer. Langrisser: Sea of Sword is developed by BlackJack Studio (the original team behind Langrisser Mobile), with a new score by composer Yasunori Nishiki. 

In Langrisser: Sea of Sword, you become the Nameless, a figure searching for lost memories from the shadows. Alongside a mysterious white-haired girl, you rise from mire and mist into a world of shifting loyalties, impossible choices, and nations standing on the brink. Across the mist-shrouded sea, hidden currents begin to stir, and a new saga unfolds.

Classic strategy is the key to breaking through the chaos. Amid the flames of war, every move, every formation, and every decision will shape the course of fate.

Langrisser: Sea of Sword is set for a global multi-platform release across iOS, Android
